entries.title: I Corinthians 13:1
segments: If I speak, etc. In this chapter the thought rises above all special manifestations of spiritual power to the pure unselfish and perfect devotion of the soul to God, the essence of whose being is love (

).  All else is inferior to this single grace.
 

 
 The tongues of men. Of all men, of every nation.
 

 
 And of angels. There is here no declaration regarding any speech of angels, but simply a comparison carried to its highest imaginative point, even to the language which angels may be supposed to speak.
 

 
 And have not love. Love in its highest reach - a pure and full affection and devotion towards God and man. See

).
 

 
 Sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. Mere empty sound.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:3
segments: Bestow. The meaning of the original word is to feed by bits or morsels, indicating the giving of all of one's means in charity to needy persons.  But even such giving might be without love (

).
 

 
 Give my body to be burned. When martyrdom came to be esteemed glorious, there were instances of persons who met it in an unchristian spirit, as is recorded of one who on his way to the stake refused to forgive one who implored his pardon.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:4
segments:
Suffereth long. With meek and undiscouraged patience under wrongs, like that of the suffering Christ.
 

 
 Is kind. Tenderly thoughtful and generous in word and act.
 

 
 Envieth not. Is not disturbed by any superiority of others.
 

 
 Vaunteth not itself. It is not boastful.
 

 
 Is not puffed up. Is not vain, proud, arrogant, or haughty.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:5
segments: Doth not behave itself unseemly. Avoids, for the sake of others, all conduct that may seem unworthy or may be a cause of reproach, such as 'the sitting at meat' in an idol's temple.  See

and notes thereon.
 

 
 Seeketh not its own. Is unselfish.
 

 
 Is not provoked. Does not readily find causes of provocation; is not irritable.
 

 
 Taketh not account of evil. Does not put it on record, as in an account book, for remembrance or revenge.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:6
segments:
Rejoiceth not in unrighteousness. Has no pleasure in prosperity or success unrighteously obtained; or, as some interpret, in hearing or telling of unrighteousness in others.
 

 
 Truth. Of doctrine, utterance, and action.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:7
segments: All things. That is, all that may be rightly borne, believed, hoped, or endured.  See

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:8
segments:
:10
 
 Love never faileth. Love is immortal as part of the heavenly life, where tongues, prophecies and human knowledge shall be superseded.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:11
segments: Childish things. The toys, the plays, and the lessons of childhood.  Like these will the highest earthly attainments seem hereafter.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:12
segments: In a mirror. The easily tarnished metallic mirror of ancient times.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:13
segments: Now abideth faith, hope, love.  They are all eternal: faith, in the forever unsearchable wisdom of God: hope, in the forever increasing glory and blessedness of heaven: love, the chief of the three, as part of the divine nature.
